question.text: Which of the following correctly describes the moratorium period in health insurance?

answer.text: After 3 continuous years of coverage, no claim can be contested by the insurer
After 5 continuous years of coverage, no claim can be contested including proven fraud
After 5 continuous years of coverage, no claim can be contested except on grounds of proven fraud and permanent exclusion
After 7 continuous years of coverage, claims become absolutely incontestable

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook page 29, the health insurance moratorium period is 5 continuous years, after which no health insurance claim shall be contestable except on grounds of proven fraud and permanent exclusion. Page 28 supports the 3-year life-insurance incontestability contrast. Page 29 also notes that if the sum insured is enhanced, the 5-year moratorium starts afresh for the enhanced limit. The Trap: Option A applies the 3-year life-insurance contestability period to health insurance. Option B drops the fraud / permanent-exclusion exception, which always remains. Option D invents a 7-year rule. Note: Distinguish the 5-year health-insurance moratorium from the 3-year life-insurance incontestability rule; the fraud and permanent-exclusion grounds always remain available to the insurer.
